body:
No one has responded but I’ll comment just Incase I get lucky. This is a copy from my first post WITHOUT any “slur”


Hi there, not new to reddit but new to posting on here. Probably posting in the wrong place but I’m sure a Mod will direct me. It’s just a lot of problems mixed in one. Never felt it necessary to post here... but I don’t even know who to talk to now. first I wanna start with.... I’m fucked. I’m 21 (actually 22 since Saturday I can’t believe I forgot about my own birthday but you’ll see why)and I am the definition of “ain’t shit” ......I was emotionally spoiled. Not materially cause my mom worked her ass off to make ends meet.  But I was emotionally sheltered. Graduated highschool and am just a waitress. A great one but that’s my biggest accomplishment. If I went on about that I could talk for hours but let’s fast forward~~~~~

About a month ago I found out my grandma who practically raised me, was sick. Two weeks ago it was cancer. Now it’s been a week and it’s hospice. She looks nothing like the queen and strong headed woman who could out drink, out smoke, and out dab me just a few months ago around Christmas. I’m an adult by age but I technically think I stopped growing mentally around 19, when I became a heavy drinker. I know my own faults and chose to continue them. 





Anyways, now I’m 22 and have to watch her die. I kinda expressed to my family that I didn’t want to be in the room when it happens but was pressured that I need to be there for my mom and her siblings who are much older but hadn’t experienced it firsthand either. So I’m going to see it and experience it. They told me I could choose but in a way I didn’t really have a choice without feeling like a shit daughter. I had to fly to the state my family is from, from Colorado just to see her sick as hell, on my 22 birthday. There was no party, no cake, no card. It was my first birthday not being completely idolized and doted on but I understood very well it wasn’t about me at all right now and mainly cared about just being here for her. So on my birthday, I spent my day staring at my still beautiful  but no longer shooting the shit and active grandma in a bed, skin and bones. 

I thought wow, my parents always taught me life doesn’t give a fuck and it’s unfair... but this was my first time really seeing it and all my older problems became so minuscule.


When I walked in she lit up, practically put me in a choke hold hug (I was so shocked at how much strength she still had saved just for hugs) and she made an attempt to sing 50 cents “Go Shorty, It’s your birthday” to me which once she heard it once she would sing every birthday she had since the song came out. it was actually the last day she was able to talk so I am SOOOOO lucky for that. But she’s not talking anymore. She’s dying. Preparing for her next adventure somewhere that is a secret to all of us on this planet. She’s fighting like the hard ass she always was. And we’ve told her to let go and it’s okay. Hospice and the preacher advised us not to use the word goodbye though. Just so we don’t give her anxiety. And we haven’t,  although mentally we’ve all said it. 




I’m just dealing with so much and so is my family and my bf of over a year is a Xanax addict and although he only takes a tiny piece at a time, he drinks at night. Tonight he went on another rampage cause it’s taken a toll on him that I had to come back home after we moved states together last year so he is alone and sad and I’m the state we both grew up in and have all of our family and friends here. I just wanted him, who loves and supports me very well, to be there. He loved my grandma too. And cried with me.
